OCT and FA are nonspecific here — as expected in early or non-proliferative sarcoid vasculopathy — and do not contradict this diagnosis. Importantly, no evidence of infection (no fever, no elevated procalcitonin, no positive serologies listed), no malignancy-specific cytopenias (e.g., no anemia or profound pancytopenia), and no neurologic symptoms reduce likelihood of lymphoma or sepsis.

- Mildly elevated serum ACE and lysozyme — supportive (though nonspecific) serologic markers of active granulomatous disease.
